turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: I came in because I feel like I’m always up and moving. Even on a quiet day, I’ll be bouncing from the garden club list to my knitting bag to travel papers, and I haven’t really finished any one thing before I’m on to the next.

symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient reports feeling 'always up and moving' and repeatedly shifting among activities before finishing them, consistent with being constantly on the go.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I do sometimes. My husband tells me I cut him off before he’s finished talking. And in group planning, I’ll jump in because I’m worried I’ll lose the thought if I don’t say it right then. It’s not that I mean to be rude, but I do it.

symptom_reasoning.S018: The patient reports cutting off her husband and jumping into group planning before others finish because she fears losing her thought.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often have trouble paying attention to details or making careless mistakes?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I do. Like when I help with papers at the community center, I’ll think I checked everything, but then I’ve missed someone’s name on the sign-up sheet or written the wrong room time on a note. It’s not all the time, but it happens enough that I notice it.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient endorses recurring careless errors in community-center paperwork, including missing names and writing incorrect room times despite checking.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I do. If I’m sitting still too long, I get this stirred-up feeling inside, like I need to get up and straighten something or go check on something. It’s not dramatic, but it’s hard to just stay put.

symptom_reasoning.S012: Patient explicitly endorses a stirred-up internal feeling when sitting still too long and an urge to get up.

turns.doctor_question: Have you always been like this, even as a child?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I think so. Even in grade school, my teachers would tell my mother I was bright but scattered. I was always losing papers, talking when I wasn’t supposed to, and wiggling around in my seat before I got my work finished.

symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient reports that they were always losing papers in grade school.
symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient describes wiggling around in their seat during grade school.
symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient reports talking when they were not supposed to at school.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever find yourself so focused on something that you lose track of everything else around you?
turns.patient_response: I’m not sure I’d say that happens much. Sometimes I get interested in something, but I don’t really lose track of everything around me in a big way.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever become so absorbed in an activity that you forget about other things you need to do?
turns.patient_response: Not really, no. I can get interested in something, but I don’t usually forget everything else I’m supposed to be doing because of it.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel like your difficulties with attention, impulsivity, and restlessness are causing problems for you at work, at home, or in your relationships?
turns.patient_response: Yes, it is. I’m not working now, but at home and at the community center it’s started to cause real strain. My husband and the other volunteers can’t really count on me to keep plans straight unless someone checks behind me, and that’s embarrassing.

symptom_reasoning.S005: She reports that her husband and other volunteers cannot rely on her to keep plans straight without someone checking behind her, indicating difficulty organizing plans and activities.

turns.doctor_question: Do you have difficulty following through on instructions or finishing tasks at the community center or at home?
turns.patient_response: I’m not really sure how to answer that. I don’t think I’ve noticed a clear pattern with instructions or finishing tasks specifically. Sometimes I need reminders, but I can’t say for sure beyond that.

turns.doctor_question: Have you experienced these difficulties with attention and impulsivity consistently throughout your life, or have there been periods where they were less noticeable?
turns.patient_response: It’s been there most of my life, I think. Even in grade school, teachers would tell my mother I was bright but scattered. I was always losing papers, talking when I shouldn’t, and fidgeting in my seat before I got my work done. So it’s not really new, no.

symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient reports that in grade school they were always losing papers.
symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient reports fidgeting in their seat during grade school.
symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient reports talking when they should not have during grade school.
symptom_reasoning.S016: Talking out of turn is strongly suggestive of blurting or speaking before it is appropriate.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel like your difficulties are affecting your relationships with your family or friends?
turns.patient_response: Yes, it has. At home it causes tension with my husband, and even with people at the community center. They can’t always count on me to keep plans straight unless someone double-checks me, and I know that gets frustrating for them.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel like your difficulties with attention and impulsivity are significantly interfering with your daily life or causing you a lot of distress?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I think it is interfering. It’s not every minute of the day, but it has started causing real strain at home and at the community center. My husband and the other volunteers can’t always count on me to keep plans straight unless someone checks behind me, and that does upset me.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient reports that others cannot reliably count on them to keep plans straight without checking behind them, indicating difficulty organizing activities.

turns.doctor_question: Do you think your impulsivity and restlessness are equally problematic for you, or does one cause more issues than the other?
turns.patient_response: The restlessness is probably the bigger issue for me. If I have to sit still too long, I get this stirred-up feeling inside, like I need to get up and straighten something or go check on something. It’s hard to just stay put.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient describes a stirred-up internal feeling when required to sit still and an urge to get up, indicating restlessness.

turns.doctor_question: Do you think you have more trouble with staying focused and paying attention or with controlling your impulses and restlessness?
turns.patient_response: I think the restlessness is harder for me. If I have to sit still too long, I get this stirred-up feeling inside, like I need to stand up and straighten something or go check on something.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient identifies restlessness as more difficult and describes an internal stirred-up urge to stand up and move when sitting still too long.

turns.doctor_question: Do you think your difficulties with paying attention or your difficulties with impulsivity and restlessness cause more problems for you in your daily life?
turns.patient_response: I’d say the restlessness causes more trouble. When I have to sit for very long, I get that stirred-up feeling inside, like I need to get up and straighten something or go check on something.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient describes an internal stirred-up urge to get up and move when required to sit for a long time, consistent with restlessness.

turns.doctor_question: Do you think your difficulties are more with not paying attention to details or with feeling restless and impulsive?
turns.patient_response: More with feeling restless, I’d say. The details can be an issue sometimes, but the thing I notice most is when I have to sit still too long, I get all stirred up inside and feel like I need to get up and straighten something or go check on something.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient identifies restlessness as the main difficulty and describes an internal stirred-up feeling when sitting still that prompts urges to get up and move.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often find yourself easily distracted by things around you?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I do. If someone’s talking in another room, or even a car passes by the window, my mind just kind of goes over to that and I lose track of what I was doing.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient explicitly endorses being distracted by nearby conversations or passing cars and losing track of the task at hand.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever become so focused on something that you can't think of anything else?
turns.patient_response: I’m not sure I’d say that happens. I can get interested in something, but I don’t usually feel like I can’t think of anything else.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever been diagnosed with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder or does anyone in your family have it?
turns.patient_response: I don’t think I’ve ever been formally diagnosed with that. And as far as family, I’m not really sure—no one that I know of talked about having it.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often struggle to complete tasks because you lose interest or get distracted?
turns.patient_response: Yes, sometimes. I’ll start out trying to pay attention, like at a planning meeting or reading the church bulletin, and after a bit I realize I’ve missed a good part of what was said or what I was reading. My mind just drifts off, I guess.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient reports initially paying attention but then missing much of a meeting or reading because their mind drifts off, indicating difficulty sustaining attention.
